patch.summary:
Choose ShipBob only if your buying job matches “Ecommerce fulfillment and logistics platform — affiliate partner in ecommerce.” rather than Spocket's shape. Choose Spocket only if your buying job matches “US/EU dropshipping sourcing app — Starter $39.99/mo, Pro $59.99/mo, Empire $99.99/mo, Unic” rather than ShipBob's shape. Workflow advantage: ShipBob leans order-fulfillment; Spocket leans dropshipping-sourcing. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: ShipBob is Ecommerce fulfillment and logistics platform — affiliate partner in ecommerce.; Spocket is US/EU dropshipping sourcing app — Starter $39.99/mo, Pro $59.99/mo, Empire $99.99/mo, Unicorn $299.99/mo; 7-day trial; product caps per tier.
- Company-size focus: ShipBob (small-business, mid-market) vs Spocket (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: ShipBob-leaning order-fulfillment vs Spocket-leaning dropshipping-sourcing.
- Researched limits: ShipBob — Requires an existing ecommerce storefront — not a cart or checkout product; Spocket — Not a storefront — requires Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, BigCommerce, or similar.

Limitations — ShipBob: Requires an existing ecommerce storefront — not a cart or checkout product; Quote-based pricing with ~$275/mo minimum reported — opaque until sales conversation; Spocket: Not a storefront — requires Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, BigCommerce, or similar; Product caps force tier upgrades as catalog grows.
